newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude steady, little direction from NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude steady, little direction from NYMEX.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures were steady after the NYMEX open and there was little chance of the June contract breaking out of its narrow range, brokers said.
June Brent traded at $18.17 at 1430 GMT having tested $18.25 and $18.30 shortly after the U.S open.
Traders said there was little fundamental news to direct the market. "We are looking for something to hold onto, but there is nothing out there," said one IPE broker.
Support was pegged at $18.05 and then $17.95.
NYMEX crude gave little impetus to a push higher. "New York has come in a touch drab," said a dealer.
June NYMEX crude was trading at $19.80, up seven cents a barrel at 1430 GMT.
Traders said $20.00 a barrel was a strong psychological barrier, but that once breached it could lead to $20.30.
The NYMEX crude delivery against the May contract was a record 6.621 million barrels, the highest level since trading began in 1983.
May IPE gas oil was trading $1.75 a tonne higher at $164.75, supported by Brent's narrowly firmer tone and by continued strong interest in Asia for diesel.
